verdict.stance: Neutral / Top-5 Global Aircraft Lessor Scaling Post-$9bn MAF Deal
verdict.summary: Dubai sovereign-owned (ICD) DAE doubled its fleet to ~1,000 aircraft via the $9.0bn acquisition of Macquarie AirFinance in July 2026. Net loans rose to $16.75bn, but net debt/equity remained disciplined at 2.60x with $5.6bn available liquidity and 88.3% unsecured funding.

positives: 100% Investment Corporation of Dubai (ICD) ownership and Baa2/BBB/BBB- investment-grade ratings.
88.3% unsecured debt share preserves unencumbered aircraft pool (~$5.6bn liquidity as of Sep-26).
Fleet scale doubled to ~1,000 aircraft post-$9bn MAF deal in tight global narrowbody supply cycle.
negatives: Net debt jumped from $10.2bn (FY25) to $16.75bn (9M26) following consecutive NAC and MAF M&A.
Higher interest rate environment weighs on lease-rate factor vs funding-cost spreads on refinancing.
Cyclical airline lessee credit risk and OEM delivery delays.
